### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via REQUEST_NOT_FOUND (literal, a string literal in registerApprovalsEndpoints))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be1ac699f5e556aebfffb9a00d08d3f80a802fa1` — the merge of head `acf67294ccc7bf52a92ac5963d4131bcd180f458` into base `968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be1ac699f5e556aebfffb9a00d08d3f80a802fa1 && git checkout be1ac699f5e556aebfffb9a00d08d3f80a802fa1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 acf67294ccc7bf52a92ac5963d4131bcd180f458 && git checkout -B drift-repro 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 && git merge --no-ff acf67294ccc7bf52a92ac5963d4131bcd180f458

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `acf67294ccc7bf52a92ac5963d4131bcd180f458`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-approvals-actions-unknown-request.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`getRequest`, `loadRequest`, `listActions`, `visibleRequestIds`, `isOverrideActor`), packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts (`IApprovalService.getRequest` / `listActions`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`registerForBase`, constructor slots, `getRoutes`), packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts (`approvals.listActions`, `fetch`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordApprovalsPanel.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts, ui/packages/core/src/adapters/ApiDataSource.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-override-composite-pin.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/27451-approvals-actions-unknown-request-404.md, PR #25628 and its changeset `.changeset/25486-unknown-resource-404.md` (the #25486 precedent)

Inputs read: cards #27451 and #27493 with every comment (triage 6491511316 and 6495966619), the PR body and file list, the net diff `481ade61..acf67294` (3 files, +174/−5), and the head's check-runs. The seat-posted os-dev report on #27451 was treated as a claim and re-derived from the diff, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The one accept-set change.** `GET {base}/approvals/requests/:id/actions` now calls `readableRequestOr404(svc, req.params.id, context, res)` before `svc.listActions`, and returns on a null row. An id the service does not hold, or a request outside the caller's visibility, answers `404 { code: 'REQUEST_NOT_FOUND', error: "Approval request 'ID' not found" }` where it answered `200 { data: [] }`. That is the triage ruling on #27451 ("404 `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`, the same as the parent door"); #27493's body said `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, and its triage folded it under #27451's ruling, which the PR follows.
- **Parent door byte-for-byte.** Before: `const row = await svc.getRequest(req.params.id, context ?? {}); if (!row) { res.status(404).json({ code: 'REQUEST_NOT_FOUND', error: \`Approval request '${req.params.id}' not found\` }); return; } res.json(row);`. After: the helper runs `svc.getRequest(id, context ?? {})` with the same arguments, writes the same `res.status(404).json({...})` literal with the same two keys, same code string and same message template, and the handler does `if (!row) return; res.json(row);`. Same status, same code, same message, no header or log line added or removed on the 404 path, same `res.json(row)` on the 200 path. A thrown `getRequest` still lands in the parent's own `catch` (`500 APPROVAL_REQUEST_GET_FAILED`, same `logError` prefix). Unchanged.
- **Existence-leak parity holds.** `ApprovalService.getRequest` is `loadRequest(id, ctx, true)`: a row `findRequestRow` does not return and a row outside `visibleRequestIds(...)` both exit through `return null`, one branch for both cases; `isOverrideActor` callers get `null` from `visibleRequestIds` and see every row. So unknown and invisible answer the same status, code and message shape, differing only in the id the caller sent. The new test pins that side by side (`unknown` vs `actions` for an outsider: equal status+code, message equal modulo the id).
- **`listActions` is never reached for an unreadable parent** (pinned `not.toHaveBeenCalled` in both 404 cases). For a readable parent the service's own gate (`listActions` → `getRequest` → `[]` on null) is unchanged, so rows still come back only when the caller can read the parent.
- **Scoped and unscoped variants.** Both handlers live in the one `registerApprovalsEndpoints` body, registered per base path by `registerForBase(basePath)` and `registerForBase(scopedBase)`; `readableRequestOr404` is a closure of that body, so both route variants share the one lookup and envelope. `environmentId` resolution precedes the lookup exactly as before.
- **Error paths unchanged.** `respond501` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) still answers before any lookup in both handlers. A `getRequest` throw inside the actions handler lands in its existing `catch` (`500 APPROVAL_ACTIONS_FAILED`); before the fix the same throw surfaced from `listActions`' internal `getRequest` through the same `catch`, so no new failure code appears.
- **The test drives the real registrar.** `new RestServer(...)` with `approvalsServiceProvider` in positional slot 12 (after the retired reports slot), `registerRoutes()`, `getRoutes()` (`rest-server.ts:6361`), handler invoked with `params: { id }`; the stub models the service's rule (`getRequest` null for unknown and for a non-participant; `listActions` gated on it). The three pins are red before `3e605bac` on the two 404 cases per the PR body, which the diff's shape makes plausible: without the helper call the handler answers `200 { data: [] }` for both.
- **Check-runs on `acf67294` as read (2026-10-29, ~23:30Z):** `success` — Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter. `in_progress` — Build Core, Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check · workspace, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Live E2E UI. `skipped` — the UI build/lint/type/test matrix, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the opt-in harnesses. No failure at read time. The landing still waits for the in-progress set to conclude green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27451-approvals-actions-unknown-request-404.md`: `'@objectstack/rest': patch` (released package, `18.2.0`, not private). Body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations, the same two lines as the PR body; the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) ...` marker in the gate's `not-required (category) why` shape; a **BREAKING** banner naming the before and after answer; an "Unchanged" paragraph for a visible request; and a "What changes for you" paragraph telling SDK callers `approvals.listActions(id)` now rejects. Nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO migration or tombstone is owed.
- Consistent with the #25486 precedent: PR #25628's changeset is the same shape line for line — `patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, BREAKING banner on a served-set narrowing, "What changes for you" via `ObjectStackClient` rejection. AGENTS.md checklist 3 (a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition) is met. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (which carries `check-adr-0087-registration`) are `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: two parent reads per actions request.** Confirmed: the REST helper runs `getRequest`, then `ApprovalService.listActions` runs `getRequest` again as its tenant gate. Judged efficiency only, as the dev said — both reads answer from the same `loadRequest`, so no correctness or leak consequence. The service gate is the defence for non-REST callers and lives in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`, outside the dispatch's file surface (`approvals-routes.ts` handler + tests + changeset); leaving it was right. See ④ should-fix 1 for the follow-up.
- **Fold.** The PR body carries `Fixes #27451` and `Fixes #27493`, matching triage 6495966619's duplicate ruling; the Claim on #27451 names the fold and the branch `claude/project-thread-kwainq`, which is the PR's head branch.
- **Skills-docs: none** — verified: `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx:368` names `client.approvals.listActions(requestId)` only; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json` reads `/actions` only for requests the clause has just created or decided (admin, visible). No doc or skill teaches the old `200 []` for an unknown id.
- **Governed surfaces:** none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`. The review is owed by the `(narrowing)` arm alone.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the service's own refusal real at the sub-resource. `ApprovalService.listActions` already decided "no readable parent → nothing"; the REST door rendered that decision as an empty audit trail, which is the one thing a consumer could misread ("this request exists and has no actions"). After the fix the door renders it with the parent's envelope. Nothing is taken away: the only callers whose answer changes are callers who cannot read the parent, who received no rows before and learn nothing new now (unknown and invisible still answer alike).

Consumers tried, in the cited code:
- `packages/client` `approvals.listActions` — `this.fetch` throws on `!res.ok` (`index.ts:7684`), so it rejects with the not-found message instead of resolving `[]`. Declared in the changeset; the same treatment #25628 gave `packages.listCommits` and `automation.listRuns`.
- Console `RecordApprovalsPanel.tsx:285` — `listApprovalActions(id).catch(() => [])` per id; ids come from `useRecordApprovals`'s request list, the same visibility rule. Unaffected.
- Console `approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` `findTimeline` — `ApiDataSource.find` throws on non-2xx; it is reached only as the related list of a request record page whose parent read came through `findRequest` → `GET /approvals/requests/:id` (same lookup), so a reader who has the page can read the timeline. An admin listing `sys_approval_request` through the data API is an override actor (`visibleRequestIds` → `null`) and sees every request's timeline. Unaffected.
- Console `approvalsApi.listActions` — no caller under `ui/apps/console/src` or `ui/packages` outside tests. Nothing to break.
- Dogfood — one reader, `approval-override-composite-pin.dogfood.test.ts:211`, the admin reading a request it opened: `200`. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` on the head. No MCP or CLI caller of the door in-repo.
- Race "visible to `listActions` but not to `getRequest`": both are the same `getRequest`; the only window is a visibility change between the REST read and the service's internal read, which yields `200 { data: [] }` from the service gate — the pre-fix answer, no leak, no new failure. The reverse (REST read null, service read visible) cannot list rows because `listActions` is not called.
- Route ledger `rest-route-ledger.ts:449` carries disposition and client name only, no response-code claim; route `metadata.summary` unchanged.

Findings:
1. **should-fix (follow-up card in `plugin-approvals`, outside this PR's surface; not blocking):** on the visible path the actions door now runs the full enriched `loadRequest` twice (REST helper, then the service gate) — `servedSubjectFields`, `enrichRows`, `attachFlowSteps`, `attachDecisionProgress` each time — and discards the first row. A cheaper visibility probe on the service, or `listActions` accepting the resolved row, removes the duplicate without weakening the non-REST gate. Efficiency only, as the dev flagged.
2. **should-fix (PR body wording only, no code change):** the body lists `approvalsApi.ts` among UI callers that "read the actions of a request they have already resolved"; `approvalsApi.listActions` has no caller in the console. The claim is harmless but not what the tree shows.

No must-fix.
